page: Amazon Web Services c5d.9xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M processor operating at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provisions 36 vCPUs across 18 physical cores using simultaneous multithreading, alongside 72.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Local storage consists of a 900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network throughput is rated at 12 Gbps.

The CPU includes hardware extensions such as AVX-512, BMI2, and AES-NI, supported by a cache layout with 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache. Standardized benchmarks place the c5d.9xlarge in the median tier for compute density, scoring 30,111.19 in PassMark CPU tests, 10,437.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 33,337.8 in multi-core stress-ng workloads. Specialized instruction throughput tests show 22,728.0 in Clang software compilation and 26,538.0 in ray tracing.

Memory benchmarks demonstrate read bandwidth of 101.84 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 44.82 GB/sec over uncached 256 MB blocks. In application benchmarks, the instance achieves 31.21 million Redis SET operations per second and 21.81 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Machine learning inference on smaller models executes at 88.67 generation tokens per second for 135M models and 10.29 tokens per second for 7B models, though prompt evaluation for large 70B models drops to 5.19 tokens per second due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware.

The c5d.9xlarge offers efficient hardware allocation for workloads that require high CPU clock speeds and low-latency ephemeral I/O without incurring the expense of surplus memory capacity. The local NVMe drive avoids network storage latency for intermediate files. Recommended workloads include distributed batch data processing, software compilation and continuous integration build nodes, video encoding pipelines, and in-memory caching tiers requiring fast scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.9xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro system. Powered by an 18-core Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M processor at 3.4 GHz, it provides 36 vCPUs, 72.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, and 900 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage with 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The compute architecture features AVX-512 vector acceleration and demonstrates solid median performance across multi-core CPU, compression, and compilation benchmarks. While lack of GPU hardware restricts large-parameter model execution, the server processes over 31 million Redis SET operations per second and offers 101.84 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Its balanced compute capacity and fast local NVMe storage make it well-suited for high-throughput batch processing, automated build systems, video encoding, and distributed caching workloads.
